en: Preface to the *Collection of Records Concerning the Translation of the Tripiṭaka*, Volume One,
compiled by Śramaṇa Sengyou.
Preface to the *Collection of Records Concerning the Translation of the Tripiṭaka*.
Now, the Absolute Truth is profoundly still and the Dharma-nature is empty and tranquil;
yet, to open the way for beings and guide the world, there is no means other than speech.
Therefore, he responded in silence through non-duality.
Gathering at the gateway of the emptiness of meaning,
he vibrates his eloquence with a single voice,
responding to the realm of all sentient beings.
Since the appearance in the world of our Teacher, the Śākyamuni,
he proclaimed his initial teachings at the Deer Park and finalized his later discourses at the Golden River.
The sūtras were used to entice those of lesser learning,
while the canonical scriptures were employed to encourage the great resolve.
The wondrous wheels distinguish the twelve divisions of the Dharma-aggregate, whose essential gateways total eighty thousand.
When the Sugata withdrew his traces,
the Arhats compiled the treasury;
first, the four Āgamas were gathered as sūtras.
In the interim, the precepts were divided into five sections;
this great treasure was therein, serving as a resource for all sentient beings.
Yet, the Way is propagated by means of people.
The Dharma manifests in dependence upon conditions;
though there is the Way, there are no people.
Thus, although the texts remain extant, none have realized them.
There are dharmas that exist without conditions;
though they coexist with one's own time, they may not be heard.
Hearing the Dharma depends upon the arrival of the opportune moment.
Awakening to the Way depends upon the arrival of the opportune moment;
only when the moment arrives does principle resonate,
and only when the time comes does transformation become pervasive.
In ancient times, when awakening arose during the Zhou dynasty, the sacred ford remained obstructed;
it was only in the Han era, with the advent of the image-teaching, that the sublime scriptures finally circulated.
Thus, the Dharma depends on conditions for its manifestation, and faith indeed finds its verification therein.
By the end of the Han dynasty, the translations by An Shigao and Yan Fotiao became increasingly clear;
at the beginning of the Wei dynasty, the commentaries and expositions by Dharmakṣema and Zhi Dun gradually flourished.
Thus, it is verified here that the Way is propagated through individuals.
Since the restoration of the Jin dynasty, the Tripitaka has become increasingly vast.
Eminent guests from foreign lands have arrived in great numbers, and among them,
wise scholars of the Central Plains have flourished with brilliant distinction.
Dashi raised its grand framework;
Dao’an and Huiyuan shook out its profound essentials.
By the banks of the Wei River, they devoted themselves to the assembly for carefree wandering.
At Mount Lu, the Prajñā Terrace was established;
herein, the attainment of true practitioners during the Semblance Dharma reached its peak.
To trace its origins, the sutras emerged from the Western Regions.
The transmission flowed toward the East;
carried across ten thousand *li*, it was translated into both Hu and Han languages,
with the national phonologies each being distinct.
Therefore, there are similarities and differences in the wording;
as it has been presented repeatedly over time,
the titles have both new and old versions.
Subsequently, few among the students of the Dharma have been able to investigate and verify these matters;
thus, scribes have followed one after another without knowing the year in which the sutra was produced,
and lecturers have stood shoulder to shoulder without discerning the person who transmitted the Dharma.
If one receives [the teachings] without being granted them, the transmission of the Way is already deficient. Indeed,
when the Sages assemble at a single time,
it is like the five matters that authenticate the scriptures.
How much more so when there has been mutual translation for a thousand years—
how could one possibly remain ignorant of the people of those times?
Formerly, Master Dao’an, with his magnificent talent and profound discernment, [perceived this].
Thereupon, a catalogue of the scriptures was compiled,
wherein what had been heard and seen was verified and clearly categorized;
from that time forward, sublime scriptures appeared at intervals.
All of these are precious oceans of the Mahāyāna, studied and recited with competition during that time;
yet as for their dates and the names of their authors, there is no one who can provide a systematic arrangement or comprehensive account.
As the years pass by, the fundamental source is on the verge of being lost;
how shall those born later dispel their doubts and find clarity?
Relying on the Dharma-gate due to my own mediocrity and shallowness,
I look up in admiration to the profound breeze of the Way and vow to propagate the Great Transformation.
Whenever dawn or dusk arrived, he would recite and uphold [the scriptures], and during the autumn and summer retreats, he would lecture and expound upon them;
there was never a time when his mind did not race toward the Garden of Amrā (Āmrapālīvana) and his spirit leap toward Vulture Peak (Gṛdhrakūṭa).
Thus, with humble resolve, he followed the current to seek its source.
I have compiled what I have heard and titled it the *Chū-sanzō-ki-shū* (Collection of Records Concerning the Tripitaka).
Part One: Records on the Origins of the Compilation.
Second, the Records of Appointments;
third, the General Prefaces to the Scriptures;
fourth, the Biographies.
By compiling the *Yuanji* (Origins and Records), the fundamental beginnings are clearly illuminated;
by collating the *Minglu* (Catalogues of Names), the chronological records do not fall into ruin;
and by summarizing the *Jingxu* (Prefaces to the Scriptures), the times of the eminent collections are sufficiently evidenced.
The biographies herein describe the character and style of these individuals;
they all delved into and analyzed the *Nanjing* (Inner Canon), examined and reflected upon external teachings,
and integrated them with their prior knowledge.
I have verified this against what was previously heard.
If there is a reliable basis for human tradition, I shall set it forth as a compass;
if the transmission of the sound is not yet detailed, the text shall remain incomplete and reserved.
Grasping the tablets and concentrating his pen, his resolve was set upon a faithful history.
Re-reading and reflecting nine times over each matter, he ensured the records were based on reality;
those with corroboration were clearly marked.
Thus, that which lacks a source will manifest of itself;
it is hoped that water from puddles and ditches will not be mixed with pure milk,
and that "swallow-stone" (ordinary jade) will not be confused with the precious jade of Chu.

However, my own knowledge is like a view through a tube; I am deeply ashamed that it lacks breadth and refinement. Should there be anything incomplete herein, I request that the wise lend me their correction. *Zhuanyuanji* (Record of the Compilation of the Origins), Scroll Ten.

*Luoyi wubai luohan chu sanzang ji* (Record of the Five Hundred Arhats Translating the Tripiṭaka from the Three Baskets), Second. *Bosha chutai jing chu bazang ji* (Record of the *Bodhisattva-tai-jing* Translated from the Eight Baskets), Third. *Hu han yijing wenzi yinyi tongyi ji* (Record of the Similarities and Differences in the Sounds and Meanings of Characters in the Chinese Translations of Indian Scriptures), Fourth. *Qianhou chu jing yi ji* (Record of the Differences Between Earlier and Later Translations of Scriptures), Fifth. 1. *Ji sanzang yuanji* (Collection of Records on the Origins of the Tripiṭaka). *Ji sanzang yuanji*, First: Regarding the compilation of the origins of the Tripiṭaka. The *Dazhidu lun* (Mahāprajñāpāramitā-śāstra) records that the Buddha entered parinirvāṇa between the twin śāla trees in the kingdom of Kuśinagara.
Lying on his bed with his head toward the north,
the heavens and earth shook,
and the hundred beasts, including lions, all let out great roars.
The devas and humans wailed;
the mountains, forests, and trees were all shattered and torn asunder.
There were immeasurable hundreds of thousands of celestial women and human women.
Sighing and sobbing, they could not restrain themselves.
Those in the three stages of training were all filled with sorrow,
while those who had attained the stage beyond training merely reflected that all phenomena are entirely impermanent.
It was only because Ānanda had not yet eliminated his personal affection and had not yet abandoned desire that his mind sank into an ocean of grief from which he could not emerge on his own.
At that time, Aniruddha spoke to Ānanda.
"You must guard the treasury of the Buddha's Dharma;
you should not, like an ordinary person, sink into an ocean of sorrow.
All conditioned phenomena possess the characteristic of impermanence."
Furthermore, the Buddha has entrusted the Dharma to you.
Now that you are distressed and have lost the task you were assigned,
you should question the Buddha.
"After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa,
how shall we practice the Path?
Who shall serve as our teacher?"
"How shall we dwell together with the ill-spoken Chanda?
What words will be uttered at the beginning of the Buddha's sutras?
Such were the various matters concerning the future."
"You should ask him. Upon hearing these words, Ānanda’s distressed mind was slightly revived,
and he regained mindfulness through the power of the Path.
At the side of the Buddha’s bed, he asked the Buddha about this matter.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Whether I am present now or after my parinirvāṇa..."
Relying on the Dharma as one's own refuge and not relying on anything else—
how does a bhikṣu rely on the Dharma as his own refuge and not rely on anything else?
He contemplates the body internally, maintains constant mindfulness and single-mindedness, brings wisdom before him, and practices with diligent effort.
He eliminates worldly greed and sorrow.
He likewise contemplates the external body and both the internal and external body.
He likewise contemplates the foundations of mindfulness regarding internal feelings, mind, and phenomena.
This is called relying on the Dharma as one's own refuge and not relying on anything else;
from now on, the Prātimokṣa Sūtra itself shall be the Great Teacher.
As it is said in the Prātimokṣa Sūtra:
One should practice bodily and verbal actions in this manner.
The bhikṣu Canda should be disciplined according to the Brahma-punishment.
If his mind becomes softened and subdued, [he shall be released].
"You should be taught the Nandaka-Kātyāyana Sūtra;
then you will be able to attain the Way.
This is the treasury of the Dharma-jewels that I have accumulated over three asaṃkhyeya kalpas."
This is what should first be stated:
"Thus have I heard: at one time the Buddha was in a certain region, in a certain country, in a certain place within a grove of trees. Why is this so?
The Buddhas of the past and future also utter these words at the beginning of their teachings;
the Buddhas of the present likewise instruct others to utter such words when they are on the verge of entering parinirvāṇa.
Even after my parinirvāṇa,
the sūtras will likewise begin with the words, "Thus have I heard.
This is because the Buddha has already entered parinirvāṇa.
Each of the great arhats, according to their own inclinations,
relinquished their bodies and entered parinirvāṇa in various places— among mountain forests, flowing springs, and river valleys.
Some flew up into the void and departed in a formation like geese,
manifesting various supernatural transformations to cause the faith and purity of mind of the multitude to be attained,
and then entered parinirvāṇa.
At that time, the gods of the six heavens of desire, up to those of the Śubhakṛtsna realm in the form realm, having witnessed this event, each thought to themselves:
"The Sun of the Buddha has set;
the radiance of his disciples—those possessed of dhyāna, samādhi, and liberation—has likewise entered parinirvāṇa."
These sentient beings suffer from various afflictions— the diseases of lust, anger, and ignorance—
and this Physician of Dharma is now about to pass swiftly into parinirvāṇa.
Who shall now provide the remedy?
The exquisite lotuses— the disciples born from within the great ocean of immeasurable wisdom—
are now once again withered and parched.
The Dharma-tree has been broken and the Dharma-clouds have dissipated;
since the Great Elephant-King of Wisdom has passed away,
the elephant-cubs likewise follow the Dharma.
The merchants having departed, from whom could they seek the treasure of the Dharma?
They gathered together and went to Mahākāśyapa;
having paid their respects, they spoke these verses in praise.
Having sighed, he said:
"Venerable sir, do you not know?
The Dharma-ship is about to break apart."
The city of the Dharma is about to collapse;
the ocean of the Dharma is about to dry up;
the banner of the Dharma is about to fall.
The lamp of the Dharma is about to go out;
those who practice the Way are gradually diminishing while the power of evil grows ever stronger.
You should establish the Buddha-dharma through great compassion.
At that time, Kāśyapa’s mind was as vast as the ocean, serene and unmoving;
after a long while, he replied:
"What you have said is indeed exactly as you have spoken."
"The world will before long be blind and shrouded in darkness through lack of wisdom.
Thereupon, Mahākāśyapa accepted the invitation in silence.
Having paid their respects, the devas departed.
Suddenly they vanished and each returned to his own place.
At that time, Kāśyapa reflected:
"How can I cause this Dharma of the Buddha, so difficult to encounter throughout three asaṃkhyeya kalpas, to remain long in the world?"
Having reflected thus, I know that this Dharma can endure for a long time;
therefore, it should be compiled in the world as the three Dharma-piṭakas: the Sūtra, the Abhidharma, and the Vinaya.
In this way, the Buddha-dharma can endure for a long time,
and people of future generations will be able to receive and practice it. Why is this so?
Throughout his lifetimes, the Buddha underwent diligent toil out of compassion for sentient beings;
having studied and attained this Dharma, he expounded it for others.
We, too, ought to receive and apply the Buddha’s teachings, proclaiming and transforming them.
After Kāśyapa had spoken these words,
he ascended to the summit of Mount Sumeru, struck the bronze ghaṇṭā,
and recited this verse:
"Disciples of all Buddhas, if you contemplate the Buddha, you should repay the Buddha's kindness and not enter nirvana.
This is the sound of the *gaṇḍī* drum, transmitting the instruction of Mahākāśyapa.
It reached throughout the trichiliocosm,
so that all those disciples who had attained supernatural powers heard and knew it.
They all came together to where Mahākāśyapa was.
At that time, Kāśyapa addressed those gathered:
"The Buddha-dharma is about to perish."
The Buddha attained this Dharma through various ascetic practices and compassion for sentient beings over three asaṃkhyeya kalpas.
After the Buddha’s parinirvāṇa,
among his disciples, there were those who knew the Dharma, upheld the Dharma, and recited the Dharma.
They all likewise entered parinirvāṇa accordingly.
The Dharma is now about to perish;
future sentient beings are truly to be pitied.
Having lost the eye of wisdom, we are ignorant and blinded by darkness.
The Buddha, out of great compassion, takes pity on sentient beings;
we ought to receive and follow the Buddha’s teachings.
"You must wait until the compilation of the Tripiṭaka is complete before entering parinirvāṇa as you please.
All those who had gathered for the assembly remained there, receiving his instruction.
At that time, Mahākāśyapa selected one thousand people,
excluding Ānanda; they were all arhats.
They have attained the six supernormal powers and are endowed with the wisdom of the three insights.
They exercise mastery over all dhyānas and samādhis, entering and emerging from them in forward, reverse, and transcendent order.
He recited and studied the Tripitaka;
he understood both internal and external scriptures,
and he was also well-versed in reading and knowing the eighteen great treatises of the various non-Buddhist schools.
They were all able to engage in debate and subdue those of other schools.
Formerly, when King Bimbisāra attained the Way,
eighty-four thousand members of his retinue also each attained the Way.
At that time, the king commanded the palace to constantly provide meals and offerings for a thousand people;
King Ajātaśatru did not discontinue this practice.
Then Mahākāśyapa reflected, saying:
"If we were to constantly beg for alms,
non-Buddhist practitioners would come forcefully to challenge us with difficult questions and cause our religious duties to be neglected.
Now, in the city of Rājagṛha, meals are regularly provided to support a thousand people."
In this place, the Dharma-piṭaka may be compiled;
for this reason, one thousand persons were selected and no more were to be taken.
At that time, Mahākāśyapa, together with one thousand people, arrived at Gṛdhrakūṭa Mountain in Rājagṛha.
He addressed King Ajātaśatru, saying:
"Provide us with food and send it to us every day;
now we shall compile the treasury of the Dharma."
One must not travel elsewhere;
this is the summer retreat of the Middle Kingdom.
On the first day of the fifteenth, the *poṣadha* (confession of precepts) is recited.
At that time, Mahākāśyapa immediately entered meditative absorption and, with his divine eye,
surveyed the assembly to see who among them possessed afflictions and should be expelled.
Only Ānanda alone had not yet passed away.
After Mahākāśyapa arose from his meditative absorption,
he took Ānanda by the hand amidst the assembly and said:
"Now that this pure assembly is compiling the Dharma-piṭaka,
you may not remain here as your fetters are not yet exhausted.
At that time, Ānanda was filled with shame and wept bitterly, thinking to himself:
"For twenty-five years I have attended upon the World-Honored One, providing for his needs;
yet never before have I experienced such suffering.
Truly, the Buddha is one of great virtue."
With compassion, mindfulness, and patience, he reflected;
having reflected, he said:
"I possess the power to attain the Way after a long time."
However, as for those who are Arhats in the Buddha-dharma,
they may not be provided with attendants or commanded to perform services;
for this reason, they leave behind residual fetters that are not completely severed.
Furthermore, it was said:
"You have another fault:
the Buddha did not intend to allow women to go forth."
Because you earnestly entreated the Buddha to permit [you] to practice the Way,
for this reason,
the True Dharma of the Buddha will decline after five hundred years.
"This is your fault.
Ānanda said, "I felt compassion for Mahāprajāpatī Gautamī."
Furthermore, the Buddhas of the three periods of time all have fourfold assemblies;
why is it that our World-Honored One alone lacks them? Moreover, it is said that when the Buddha was about to enter nirvana, he was near the city of Kuśinagara.
At that time, the Buddha suffered from back pain;
he folded his uttarāsaṅga robe four times, spread it out as a bed,
and said to you:
"I required water,
yet you did not provide it;
this is your fault."
Ānanda said, "At that time,
five hundred carts crossed the stream, making the water turbid;
for this reason, I did not take it."
Furthermore, it is said:
"Even if the water were turbid,
the Buddha possesses great supernatural powers."
"It can cause the turbid waters of the great ocean to become pure and clear.
Why do you not give it to me?
He spoke again:
The Buddha asked you:
"If there were someone who had well cultivated the four bases of psychic power,
they could remain in the world for an eon, or slightly less than an eon."
The Buddha’s cultivation of the four bases of psychic power is supreme;
he could remain in the world for an eon, or slightly less than an eon,
yet you remained silent and did not answer.
Thus he asked a second and a third time,
and you remained silent.
Had you answered the Buddha, his supernormal powers being well-cultivated, he would have remained in the world for a full kalpa or slightly less than a kalpa.
It is precisely because of you that the World-Honored One has entered parinirvāṇa prematurely;
this is your fault.
Ānanda said, "Māra obscured my mind;
for this reason, I remained silent."
"It is not that I have a malicious mind that I do not answer the Buddha.
Kāśyapa spoke again:
"You should fold the saṃghāṭī robe for the Buddha."
"You stepped upon it with your foot;
this is your fault," Ānanda said.
At that time, a great wind suddenly arose and there was no one to help me;
the wind blew it here so that it fell at my feet.
It was not out of a lack of reverence that I stepped upon the Buddha’s robe.
Furthermore, it is said:
"The Buddha displayed his mark of the concealed organ (*kośagatavastiguhyatā*) to women after his parinirvāṇa;
how could this be anything but shameful?"
"This is your fault.
Ānanda said, "At that time, I thought:"
If any women were to see the Buddha’s mark of the concealed organ,
they would immediately feel ashamed of their female form and aspire to attain a male body.
I manifest this because I cultivate the marks of a Buddha through the accumulation of meritorious karma;
it is not for the sake of shamelessness that I break the precepts.
Mahākāśyapa said,
"You have committed six offenses;
you ought to repent before the Saṃgha."
Ānanda replied, “I accept.
He respectfully followed the instructions of Mahākāśyapa and the Saṃgha.

At that time, Ānanda knelt with his palms joined, bared his right shoulder, removed his leather sandals, and performed the confession of the six transgressions; having finished the confession, he stood.
Mahākāśyapa again took Ānanda by the hand and led him out from among the Saṃgha,
saying to Ānanda: "Only after you have severed your outflows and attained their exhaustion shall you come back in."
"Since your residual fetters are not yet exhausted, do not come here.
Having spoken these words,
he then shut the door himself.
At that time, the arhats deliberated, saying,
"Who is capable of compiling the Dharma-piṭaka? Aniruddha said:
Śāriputra, this was the second of the Buddha’s excellent disciples.
His name was Gavāmpati;
he was gentle, harmonious, and elegant, always dwelling in seclusion and well-versed in the treasury of the Dharma.
"He is currently in the Śirīṣa Tree Garden in the heavens;
you may dispatch a messenger to invite him.
Mahākāśyapa then spoke to a junior monk seated below.
Next, you should go as a messenger of the Sangha to the Śirīṣa tree grove in the heavens, to the dwelling place of Gavāmpati.
Having arrived, speak to Gavāmpati:
"Mahākāśyapa is an Arhat whose outflows are exhausted."
All shall assemble in Jambudvīpa;
the Saṃgha has a great Dharma-affair.
You should come quickly.
The bhikṣu joyfully and respectfully accepted the Sangha’s command;
he prostrated with his head at the feet of the Sangha, circumambulated them three times to the right,
and departed like a garuḍa soaring through the sky.
Having arrived, he prostrated at his feet and said,
"Mahākāśyapa has a message:
there is now a great Dharma-affair for the Saṃgha."
"You should come quickly to behold this multitude of various jewels.
At that time, Gavāmpati felt doubt in his heart and spoke to the bhikṣu, saying:
"Has the Saṃgha summoned me because of some matter of dispute? Is there no one who is causing a schism in the Saṃgha?
Has the Buddha-Sun not yet entered parinirvāṇa?
Thus spoke that bhikṣu.
"It is exactly as you have said.
The Great Teacher, the World-Honored One, has already entered parinirvāṇa. Gavāmpati then spoke.
The Buddha has passed into parinirvāṇa too soon;
the Eye of the World has been extinguished.
The Great General who followed the Buddha in turning the Wheel of Dharma—
"Where is my preceptor Śāriputra now?
He replied,
"He entered parinirvāṇa previously."
Gavāmpati said, "The Great Master and the generals of the Dharma are each departing separately;
what can be done about it?"
"Where is Mahāmaudgalyāyana now? He replied,
"He too has already entered parinirvāṇa."
Gavāmpati said: "The Buddha-dharma is about to disperse;
the Great Man has passed away."
“Beings are to be pitied.
Elder Ānanda, what are you doing now?
He replied:
The bhikṣu Ānanda was filled with grief and wept, unable to compose himself.
Gavāmpati said, "Ānanda’s distress arises from the fetter of craving; it is born of the suffering of separation."
"What about Rāhula? [The Buddha] replied,
"Because he has attained arhatship, he has neither sorrow nor grief."
He simply contemplated the characteristic of impermanence in all phenomena. Gavāmpati said,
"Because he has been able to sever the love that is so difficult to cut."
Furthermore, he said:
"I have lost my Great Teacher, the World-Honored One,
in whom I had dwelt."
Furthermore, for what purpose would I do so?
My preceptor and great master have already entered parinirvāṇa;
I am currently unable to descend to Jambudvīpa.
"I shall now enter parinirvāṇa right here.
Having spoken these words, he immediately entered meditative absorption,
rose into the air, and manifested various miraculous transformations, emitting light from his body.
He emitted fire from his own body and burned it,
while water issued forth from within his body and flowed down in four streams until he reached the place where Mahākāśyapa was.
From within the water, a voice spoke this verse:
"Kubjottara bows his head in homage to the Great Virtuous Saṅgha, the most excellent among the wondrous multitude.
Hearing that the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa, I shall follow him; just as when a great elephant departs, the elephant calf follows."
The junior bhikṣu took the robes and bowl and returned them to the Saṅgha.
During this interval, Ānanda contemplated and sought the exhaustion of his remaining fetters;
he sat in meditation and practiced walking meditation, diligently seeking the Way.
This Ānanda has much wisdom but little concentration;
therefore, he does not immediately attain the Way.
Only when concentration and wisdom are equal can one quickly attain it.
As the latter part of the night was drawing to a close,
being utterly exhausted, he lay down to rest and turned onto his pillow;
before his head had even reached the pillow, he attained a sudden and profound awakening.
Just as one who sees the path when a flash of lightning emerges from the darkness,
so too, Ānanda, has he entered the diamond-like concentration (vajropamasamādhi) and shattered the mountain of all afflictions (kleśa).
He attained the three knowledges and the six supernormal powers,
was endowed with the eight liberations,
and became a powerful Arhat.
That very night, he arrived at the door of the Sangha hall and knocked,
calling out. Mahākāśyapa asked,
"Who is knocking at the door?"
He replied, "I am Ānanda.
He asked again.
"Why have you come? he asked, to which [the other] replied, "Tonight I have attained the exhaustion of all outflows (āsravakṣaya).
He further said:
"I will not open the door for you;
come through the keyhole of the door.
Ānanda said, "So be it."
He immediately used his supernatural power to enter through a non-door,
prostrated at the feet of the Sangha,
and repented. Mahākāśyapa said:
"Do not reproach me further.
Mahākāśyapa stroked his head with his hand, saying,
'It was for your sake that I caused you to attain the Way.'"
"You have no resentment;
I am likewise. Because you have realized this for yourself—just as one might draw upon empty space with the hand, leaving it entirely unstained."
The mind of an Arhat is also like this.
Return to your original seat.
At that time, the assembly again deliberated together, saying:
"Gavāmpati has already entered parinirvāṇa;
who else is capable of compiling the Dharma-piṭaka? Aniruddha said:
This Elder Ānanda is one who constantly attends upon and stays close to the Buddha among the Buddha’s disciples;
he is able to retain the sūtras he hears, and the Buddha frequently praises him.
It was Ānanda alone who compiled the Dharma-piṭaka.
At that time, Mahākāśyapa placed his hand upon Ānanda’s head and said,
"The Buddha entrusted you with the charge to uphold the Dharma-piṭaka."
"You should repay the Buddha’s kindness.
Where did the Buddha first preach the Dharma?
And who among the Buddha’s great disciples are capable of guarding the treasury of the Dharma?"
All have already entered parinirvāṇa;
you alone remain. You should now follow the Buddha’s intention and, out of compassion for sentient beings, compile the treasury of the Dharma.
At that time, after Ānanda had paid homage to the Saṃgha,
he sat upon the lion throne.
Then Mahākāśyapa spoke this verse:
The Buddha is the Holy Lion-King; Ānanda is his son. Seated upon the lion throne, he surveys the assembly, yet there is no Buddha.
Such a multitude of great virtues has lost its majestic power, like the sky when the moon is absent;
though the constellations remain, they lack their splendor. O you of great wisdom!

*Ānāpāna-śīyi-jīng* (Sūtra on the Guarding of the Mind through Ānāpāna), one fascicle; the An-lu (An’s Catalog) states it is the *Xiǎo-ānāpāna-jīng*. *Yīn-chí-rù-jīng* (Sūtra on the Bases of Mental Application and the Elements), one fascicle.
*Bǎi-liù-shí-pǐn-jīng* (Sūtra in One Hundred and Sixty Chapters), one fascicle; the Old Catalog states it consists of one hundred and sixty chapters from the *Ekottarika Āgama*.

*Dà-shí-èr-mén-jīng* (Great Sūtra on the Twelve Gates), one fascicle. *Xiǎo-shí-èr-mén-jīng* (Small Sūtra on the Twelve Gates), one fascicle. *Dà-dào-dì-jīng* (Sūtra on the Stages of the Great Path), two fascicles; attributed to Master Dao’an.

The *Daodizhi jing* (Sūtra on the Stages of the Great Path) is an excerpt from the *Xiuxing jing* (Sūtra on the Practice of the Way). There is one fascicle of the *Renben yusheng jing* (Sūtra on the Human Roots for Rebirth), translated by a foreigner;
two fascicles of the *Daoyi faxing jing* (Sūtra on the Arising of the Resolve for Enlightenment); and one fascicle of the *Abidamo wufa jing* (Abhidharma Sūtra on the Five Dharmas).
The old catalog states it is the *Abidamo wufaxing jing*. There is also one fascicle of the *Qifa jing* (Sūtra on the Seven Dharmas); the old catalog states it is the *Abidamo qifaxing jing*.
In some versions of the *Sūtra*, it is called the *Saptadharmapratipatti* (Sevenfold Practice); this [version] is currently missing.

The *Pañcadharmasūtra* (One fascicle) and the *Daśavārāṇasūtra* (Two fascicles)—the old catalogs state that the *Dīrghāgama Daśavārā-dharmapratipatti-sarvavidhisūtra* (One fascicle), also known as the *Sarvadharmapratipatti-sarvavidhi*—have the *Sarvadharmapratipatti* as its author and the *Sarvavidhi* as the author of the *Śāriputra*; all other meanings are consistent with the *Vinayārthaviniścaya*.

One fascicle; alternatively called the *Yijue* (Decisions on Meaning). Regarding the *Lüfaxing jing* (Sūtra on the Practice of the Vinaya Dharma), Master Dao’an stated that these two preceding sūtras are from the *Dīrgha Āgama*.

Currently, they are missing. The *Fenbu jing* (Sūtra on the Distribution [of the Four Elements]), one fascicle; the *Sidi jing* (Sūtra on the Four Noble Truths), one fascicle. Master Dao’an stated that these two preceding sūtras are from the *Dīrgha Āgama*.

The *Qichu san guan jing* (Sūtra on the Seven Stations and Three Contemplations), two fascicles; the *Jiu heng jing* (Sūtra on the Nine Sudden Deaths), one fascicle; the *Bazhengdao jing* (Sūtra on the Eightfold Noble Path).
One fascicle. Master Dao’an states that the three aforementioned sutras are extracted from the *Saṃyukta Āgama* and the forty-fourth chapter of the *Saṃyukta Sūtra*.
Two fascicles. Master Dao’an states these are extracted from the *Ekottara Āgama*; as their specific titles are not indicated, it is unclear which sutras they belong to.

Currently missing: the *Wǔshí Jiàojì Jīng* (Sutra on the Fifty Calculations) in two fascicles; some call it the *Míngdù Wǔshí Jiàojì Jīng*. The *Dà Ānban Jīng* (Great Anapanasmati Sutra) in one fascicle.

*Siwei jing* (Sūtra on Contemplation), one fascicle; alternatively, *Siwei lüyào fǎ* (The Essential Method of Contemplation); *Shí'èr yīnyuán jīng* (Sūtra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination), one fascicle;
*Wǔyīn yù jīng* (Sūtra of Similes for the Five Aggregates), one fascicle—the old catalog calls it *Wǔyīn pìyù jīng* (Sūtra of Similes for the Five Aggregates);

*Zhuǎnfǎlún jīng* (Sūtra on Turning the Wheel of Dharma), one fascicle—alternatively called *Fǎlún zhuǎn jīng* (Sūtra on the Turning of the Wheel of Dharma) or *Liúshè jīng* (Sūtra on the Flowing Collection)—the old catalog calls it *Yīqiè liú jīng* (Sūtra on All Flows), or alternatively, *Yīqiè...* [incomplete].
*Liusheshoushoujing* (The Sutra on Flowing and Guarding the Precepts), one fascicle; *Fafafeijing* (The Sutra on Dharma and Non-Dharma), one fascicle;

*Shisiyijing* (The Sutra on the Fourteen Intentions), one fascicle—the old catalog states this is the *Bodhisattva Shisiyijing*, but the current text is missing; *Xiangyichijing* (The Sutra on the Causes of Mutual Dependence), one fascicle;
*Angong yun chuzhongaham* (Master An says it is from the Madhyama Āgama); *Axingkouxiejing* (The Sutra of Aṅgīrasa’s Oral Explanation), one fascicle—some say it is the *Aṅgīrasa Kouxie*.
The *Sūtra on the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination* (also known as the *Sūtra on Severing the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination*).

The *Record of Old Sūtras* states that there were four titles for this single text based on the oral explanations of Marquis An. The *Abhidharma Sūtra on the Ninety-eight Bonds*, one fascicle; currently missing.

The *Sūtra on the Dhyāna Practice of Conceptualization*, one fascicle; currently missing. The *Sūtra of Nandika the Householder*, one fascicle; currently missing. The above total is thirty-four [texts].
In forty fascicles. During the reign of Emperor Huan of the Han dynasty.
Translated by the śramaṇa An Shigao of the Parthian Kingdom.
Its oral explanation of the Four Noble Truths consists of fourteen sections and ninety-eight knots;
this is the work of Master An.
It is said that this was compiled by Lokakṣema.

*The Sūtra of the Practice of the Way* (Dàoxíng jīng), one fascicle; Master Dao’an stated that the *Dàoxíng pǐn jīng* is an excerpt from the *Prajñāpāramitā*. It was compiled by a person of high wisdom from the Western Regions, and Master Dao’an composed its preface and commentary. This constitutes one work.
It consists of one fascicle.
During the reign of Emperor Huan of the Han dynasty,
the Indian śramaṇa Zhu Shuofu brought the Indic manuscript to China.
During the reign of Emperor Ling,
he translated at Luoyang the *Daoxing pin jing* (Sūtra on the Practice of the Way) in ten fascicles— also known as the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra*— or in eight fascicles.
On the eighth day of the tenth month in the second year of Guanghe, two fascicles of the *Śūraṃgama-samādhi Sūtra* were produced.
On the eighth day of the twelfth month in the second year of Zhongping, one fascicle of the *Pratyutpanna-buddha-saṃmukhāvasthita-samādhi Sūtra* was produced; it is missing today.

An old catalog states that the *Mahā-pratyutpanna-samādhi Sūtra* was produced on the eighth day of the tenth month in the second year of Guanghe. Two fascicles of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-avadāna* (or *Tuṇḍanatarasūtra*) were produced.
The *Jiulù* (Old Catalogue) states: The *Zhēnduóluówáng jīng* (Sūtra of King Candra) is recorded in the *Bièlù* (Separate Catalogue) but is missing from the present-day *Ān lù* (Catalogue of An).

In the "Ancient Section" of the *Fāngděng bù* (Vaipulya Section), it says: *Yírì shuō bānrě jīng* (One Scroll, Sūtra Spoken by the Sun’s Departure), now missing; *Guānmíng sānmèi jīng* (One Scroll, Sūtra on the Samādhi of Radiance), appearing in the *Bièlù* but not in the *Ān lù*.
The *Āshéshìwáng jīng* (Two Scrolls, Sūtra of King Ajātaśatru) was stated by Master Ān to have been excerpted from the *Cháng āhán* (Dīrgha Āgama).
The *Aśoka-rāja-sūtra* (contained in the old catalog); the *Ratnakūṭa-sūtra*, one fascicle—Master An says it is also titled the *Maṇiratnaprabhāsa*;
translated in the second year of the Huangchu era. The old catalog says it is the *Maṇiratna-sūtra*, two fascicles;
the *Praśnavyākaraṇa-sūtra*, one fascicle—Master An says it belongs to the Vaipulya section; some say it is the *Mañjuśrī-paripṛcchā-bodhisattva-praśnavyākaraṇa-sūtra*; the *Huparīnirvāṇa-sūtra*.

*Jinque Dousha jing* (The Sūtra on the Present Absence of the *Tousha*), one fascicle; *Achufo guo jing* (The Sūtra on the Land of Akṣobhya Buddha), one fascicle—also called *Achufo cha zhu pusa xuecheng pin jing* (The Sūtra on the Chapter on the Training of Bodhisattvas in the Realm of Akṣobhya Buddha) or *Achufo jing* (The Sūtra of Akṣobhya Buddha); *Bo ben jing* (The Original Sūtra of Pai), two fascicles, now missing;
*Neizang baipin jing* (The Sūtra of One Hundred Items from the Inner Treasury), one fascicle. Master Dao’an stated it was extracted from the Vaipulya section; old catalogs state it is from the *Nei*.

The *Zhàng bǎibǎo jīng* (Sūtra of the Hundred Treasures Stored Within) is found throughout various catalogs; since it contains the "Hundred Treasures Stored Within" and not a "Hundred Items Stored Within," we know it is this very sūtra.
The above constitutes thirteen sections.
It consists of twenty-seven fascicles in total and was translated by the Śramaṇa Zhi Chen from the country of Yuezhi during the reigns of Emperors Huan and Ling of the Han dynasty.
From the *Gupin* (Ancient Chapters) down to the *Neizang baimin pin* (One Hundred Chapters on Inner Treasures), there are nine scriptures in total.
Master Dao’an stated that these appear to have been translated by Zhi Chen.

*Chengju guangming jing* (Sūtra on the Attainment of Complete Radiance), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Chengju guangming sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Samādhi of Complete Radiance) or *Chengju guangming dingyi jing* (Sūtra on the Concentration of Complete Radiance).
This work consists of one fascicle in total.
During the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty, Zhi Yao translated the *Fajing jing* (Dharmādarśa-sūtra), one fascicle.

Master Dao’an stated that the *Fangdeng jing Shihui* (The Ten Wisdoms of the Vaipulya Sūtras), one fascicle, was also produced by him; some say it is the *Śrāmaṇera-daśajñāna*. These two works constitute a pair.
It consists of two fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Ling of the Han dynasty,
the śramaṇa Yan Fotiao and the Commandery Governor An Xuan translated it together.
The *Shihhui* (Ten Wisdoms) was compiled by Fo-diao.
The *Zhongbenqijing* (Sutra on the Origin of the Middle Period) in two fascicles, also known as the *Taizi Zhongbenqijing* (Sutra on the Origin of the Middle Period of the Prince);
this one work consists of two fascicles in total.
During the Jian’an era of Emperor Xian of the Han dynasty,
Kang Mengxiang translated the *Dharmapada Sūtra* in two fascicles. This constitutes one work.
It consists of two fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Wen of the Wei dynasty,
the Indian śramaṇa Viśuddhananda [brought it].
In the third year of the Huangwu era of Sun Quan, the Ruler of Wu, the Hu original was brought forth;
Zhu Jiangyan and Zhi Qian of Wuchang translated it together.
The *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra* in two fascicles is complete, while the *Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra* in two fascicles is missing. Master Dao’an stated that it was extracted from the *Dīrgha Āgama*.
According to the records of Han You, the present *Dīrgha Āgama* differs from these;

there are two fascicles of the *Sūtra of Auspicious Responses and Original Arisings*, two fascicles of the *Minor Aśokasūtra*, one fascicle of the *Huiyin jing* (also known as the *Huiyin Samādhi Sūtra* or the *Practical Application of Huiyin Samādhi Sūtra*), and one fascicle of the *Benye jing* (also known as the *Bodhisattva Benye Sūtra*). [There is also] the *Dharmapada*.
*Sūtra* in two fascicles; *Sūrala-sūtra* in one fascicle (also called *Sūrala-bodhisattva-sūtra*); *Brahmayu-sūtra* in one fascicle;
*Śyāmaka-sūtra* in one fascicle (alternatively written as *Śyāh-mei*; this sūtra is identical to the *Bodhisattva-dao-shu-jing*);
*Vimala-dhāraṇī-sūtra* in one fascicle (also called *Amitābha-anantamukha-vimala-dhāraṇī-sūtra*).
Within two fascicles of the *Sūtra*, the titles are given as: *The Sūtra of Amitābha, the Samyak-saṃbuddha, the Sarvadarśin, Who Transcends the Human Path*;
*The Sūtra of the Youth Candraprabha* (one fascicle), also known as *The Sūtra of the Boy Candraprabha* or *The Sūtra on the Samādhi of the Bodhisattva Candraprabha*;
*The Sūtra of the Meaning-Sufficient* (two fascicles); *The Sūtra of the Four Matters of Ānanda*; and *The Sūtra of Kṣemaka*.
*The Sūtra of Mātṛ Udāra*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Seven Missing Daughters*, one fascicle;
Ān Shìgāo states it is extracted from the *Aṣṭa-ācārya-abhidharma-sūtra*; *The Sūtra of Śreṇika*, one fascicle; Ān’s catalog states it is extracted from the *Madhyama-āgama*;
*The Pilu (Vidura) Excerpted Sūtra*, one fascicle—this current *Pilu Sūtra* in one fascicle is the same as the four-fascicle *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, though some call it the *Mahā-*.
*The Sutra on the Perfection of Wisdom for the Old Woman*, one fascicle; Master An states it is extracted from the *Abhidharma-śīla-sūtra*.
*The Sutra on the Four Vows*, one fascicle; missing. *The Sutra on Repentance*, one fascicle; some say it is the "Preface to the Text on the Ten Directions’ Rites of Repentance.
*The Sutra on the Virtue of the Worthy One*, one fascicle. *The Thirty Verses on the Buddha’s Past Conduct*, one fascicle; missing.

*Ben sheng si jing* (Sūtra on the Fundamental Cycle of Birth and Death), one fascicle. Master An stated it was the *Chusheng jing* (Sūtra on the Arising of Life). Xu’s examination shows that the five-fascicle *Sheng jing* does not contain this title;

only the *Ming ershi ji jing* (Sūtra of the Twenty Verses on Illumination) in one fascicle remains. *Shoulengyan jing* (Śūraṅgama Sūtra), two fascicles, recorded in the *Bielu* (Separate Catalog) but absent from Master An’s catalog;

currently missing. *Longshi nü jing* (Sūtra of the Dragon-Giving Daughter), one fascicle, recorded in the *Bielu* but absent from Master An’s catalog. *Fajing jing* (Dharma-Mirror Sūtra), two [fascicles].
The scroll is extracted from the *Bielu* (Separate Record). The *Anlu* (An Shigao’s Record) lacks one scroll of the *Luzi jing* (Mṛgāra-sūtra), which is included in the *Bielu*.
The *Anlu* lacks one scroll of the *Shiermen dafangdeng jing* (Dvādaśamukha-mahāvaipulya-sūtra), which is included in the *Bielu*.

The *Anlu* lacks the current missing one scroll of the *Latuoheluo jing* (Rāṣṭrapāla-sūtra), which is included in the *Bielu*; it is also referred to as the *Luohan Latuoheluo jing* (Arhat Rāṣṭrapāla-sūtra).
The above consists of thirty-six sections and forty-eight fascicles.
[They were translated] during the reign of Emperor Wen of the Wei dynasty.
Translated by Zhi Qian from the beginning of the Huangwu era of Sun Quan, the ruler of Wu, until the Jianxing era of Sun Liang;

the *Liudu ji jing* (Collection of the Six Pāramitās) in nine fascicles—also called the *Liudu wuji jing*, *Du wuji ji*, or *Za wuji jing*—and the *Wu pin* (Five Chapters) in five fascicles, comprising ten chapters in total, of which the latter two sections are currently missing.
It consists of fourteen fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Ming of the Wei dynasty,
the Indian śramaṇa Kang Senghui [translated it].
During the reigns of the Wu rulers Sun Quan and Sun Liang, the following were translated:

the *Śūraṃgama-samādhi Sūtra* in two fascicles (incomplete), the *Sūrya-paripṛcchā Sūtra* in one fascicle (incomplete), and the *Ātānāṭīya Sūtra* in one fascicle (incomplete). These constitute the three sections on the right.
It consists of four fascicles in total and was translated by Bai Yan during the reign of Emperor Gaogui of the Wei dynasty.
As recorded in the *Bielu* (Separate Catalog):
the name of this work was not previously included in Master Dao’an’s catalog.

The twenty-fascicle *Fangguang jing* (Prakāśa-prātihārya-sūtra) appeared on the fifteenth day of the fifth month of the first year of the Yuankang era of the Jin dynasty; it contains ninety chapters and is also known as the *Jiu xiaopin* (Old Shorter Version). One copy of this section is missing.
It consists of twenty fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Gaogui of the Wei dynasty,
the śramaṇa Zhu Shixing...
In the fifth year of the Ganlu era, he arrived at the kingdom of Khotan and transcribed this scripture—
the authentic Sanskrit text in Hu script— in nineteen chapters.
He reached [China] at the beginning of the Yuankang era of Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty.
Translated at the South Temple on the Cangheng River in Chenliu.
The *Prajñāpāramitā-sūtra* (Guangzan jing), ten fascicles and seventeen chapters, was produced on the twenty-fifth day of the eleventh month in the seventh year of the Taikang era.
The *Bhadrakalpika-sūtra*, seven fascicles; the old catalogs refer to it as the *Bhadrakalpa-samādhi-sūtra* or the *Bhadrakalpa-samāpatti-sūtra*.
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month in the first year of Yuankang, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* in ten fascicles and twenty-seven chapters was translated.
The old catalogs state that it is called the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* or the *Vaipulya-saddharmapuṇḍarīka*.

On the tenth day of the eighth month in the seventh year of Taikang, the *Lalitavistara-sūtra* in eight fascicles and thirty chapters was translated. Master Dao’an stated that it belongs to the Vaipulya section.

In the fifth month of the second year of the Jià era, the *Mahākaruṇā-sūtra* (Dà'āi jīng) in seven fascicles and twenty-eight chapters was translated. An older catalogue states it is the *Tathāgata-mahākaruṇā-sūtra*.
On the seventh day of the seventh month of the first year of the Yuánkāng era, the *Lokānuvartana-sūtra* (Dùshì pǐn jīng) in six fascicles was translated;

some say it is the *Dùshì*, or that it consists of five fascicles. On the thirteenth day of the fourth month of the first year of the Yuánkāng era, the *Guhyakādhipati-sūtra* (Mìjì jīng) in five fascicles was translated.

The scroll is also called the *Mijiji Jingang Lishi Jing* (Sūtra of the Secret-Karma Vajra-mighty-one), or in seven scrolls. On the eighth day of the tenth month of the ninth year of Taikang, the six-scroll *Chixin Jing* (Sūtra of Holding the Mind) was produced;
it consists of seventeen chapters and is also named *Dengyu Zhufa* (Equal Mastery of All Dharmas) or *Zhuangyan Fofa* (Adornment of the Buddha-dharma).

The old catalogues call it the *Chixin Fantian Jing* (Sūtra of the Brahma-deva Holding the Mind), or the *Chixin Fantian Suowen Jing* (Sūtra of the Questions of the Brahma-deva Holding the Mind). Ta...
On the tenth day of the third month in the seventh year of the Taikang era, the *Xiuxing jing* (Sutra on the Practice of the Path) in seven fascicles and twenty-seven chapters was translated.
An old catalog states that the *Xiuxing daodi jing* (Sutra on the Stages of Cultivating the Path) was translated on the twenty-third day of the second month in the fifth year of Taikang.

On the twenty-first day of the eleventh month in the seventh year of Yuankang, the *Jianbei yiqiezhi jing* (Sutra on the Gradual Preparation for All-Knowledge) in ten fascicles—or perhaps five—was produced.
The *Sāgaranāgarājaparipṛcchā-sūtra* in five fascicles, or four fascicles; the *Sāgaranāgarājaparipṛcchā-sūtra* in four fascicles, or three fascicles.
On the tenth day of the seventh month of the sixth year of Taikang, the *Puchao jing* (Sūtra of Universal Transcendence) in four fascicles was produced—also known as the "Ajātaśatru-rāja-parivarta.

An’s catalog likewise states it was also produced as the *Ajātaśatru-rāja-sūtra*, or in three fascicles. Old catalogs state that its contents consist of the Mañjuśrī-pūrvayoga and the Samādhi of Universal Transcendence.
On the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month of the seventh year of Taikang, one fascicle of the *Vimalakīrti-sūtra* was produced;
another version states it is titled the *Sūtra on Explaining the Non-retrogression of Vimalakīrti* in four fascicles.

On the fourteenth day of the tenth month of the fifth year of Taikang, two fascicles of the *Sūtra on Adorning the Pure Buddha-land* were produced; the old catalog records it as the *Mañjuśrī-adornment*.
The *Jing jing* (Pure Sūtra), also known as the *Wenshu fotu yanjing jing* (Sūtra on the Adornment and Purity of Mañjuśrī’s Buddha-field) or the *Anouda jing* (Anavatapta Sūtra) in two fascicles;

alternatively titled the *Hongdao guangxian sanmei jing* (Sūtra on the Extensive Manifestation of the Samādhi of Propagating the Way); old catalogs refer to it as the *Anouda longwang jing* (Sūtra of the Anavatapta Dragon King) or the *Anouda qingfo jing* (Sūtra Requested by the Anavatapta [King]).
The *Shoulengyan jing* (Śūraṅgama Sūtra) in two fascicles, a different recension, begins with Ānanda speaking. The *Wuliangshou jing* (Sukhāvatīvyūha Sūtra).
*The Sūtra of the Immeasurable Pure and Equal Enlightenment*, two fascicles; also known as *The Treasure Store Sūtra*, two fascicles.
The old catalogues state it is either *The Mañjuśrī Treasure Store Sūtra* or *The Manifestation of the Mañjuśrī Treasure Store*. Translated in the tenth month of the sixth year of the Taishi era.
*The Jewel-Knot Sūtra*, two fascicles; also known as *The Sūtra on the Pure Conduct of Bodhisattvas*. The old catalogues state it is the *Jewel-Knot*.

The *Bodhisattva Sūtra*, also known as the *Sūtra of the Questions of Bodhisattva Ratnakūṭa*; translated on the fourteenth day of the seventh month in the first year of the Yongxi era (502 CE), consisting of two fascicles;
also known as the *Sūtra of the Essential Collection of All Buddhas* (*Sarvabuddhasamuccaya-sūtra*). The Indian title is *Buddhasaṃgīti*.
The *Sūtra of the Chapter on the Buddha’s Ascent to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven*, in two fascicles; and the *Sūtra of the Samādhi of the Collection of All Virtues*, in three fascicles.
The *Jiulù* (Old Catalogue) states: *Dengji zhongde jīng* (Sūtra on the Collection of All Virtues), also called *Dengji wujinyi jīng* (Sūtra on the Collection of Akṣayamati), four fascicles;

*Lijushinü jīng* (Sūtra of the Girl Vimaladattā), one fascicle; *Yujia changzhe jīng* (Sūtra of the Householder Ugga), translated on the second day of the twelfth month of the tenth year of the Dàkāng era, one fascicle—also called *Yujialuoyue wen pusa xing jīng* (Sūtra of the Questions of the Householder Uggarāta on the Conduct of Bodhisattvas), which is the same as the *Dayujia jīng* (Great Ugga Sūtra). Or it is [recorded as]...
*The Scripture on the Dharma-Gate of Great Purity*, two fascicles; one fascicle [of this work] was produced on the twenty-sixth day of the third month in the first year of the Jiānshǐ era.
*The Scripture on the Son of Heaven Susatya*, two fascicles; produced in the eleventh month of the second year of the Tàishǐ era. *The Scripture on the Illusionist Rénxián*, one fascicle;
also called *The Scripture on Rénxián the Illusionist* or *The Scripture on Māra’s Rebellion*; produced in the twelfth month of the tenth year of the Tàikāng era.

*Yue-er-chu-chi-zhu-fang-deng-jing* (The Scripture on the Moon’s Second-Day Salvation of All Vaipulya [Teachings]), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Ji-zhu-fang-deng-xue-jing* (The Scripture on Saving Those Studying All Vaipulya).

*De-guang-tai-zai-jing* (The Scripture of Prince De-guang), one fascicle; alternatively titled *Lai-ta-huo-luo-suo-wen-guang-de-tai-zai-jing* (The Scripture of the Questions of Rāṣṭrapāla Regarding Prince De-guang).

*Wen-shu-shi-li-jing-lü-jing* (The Scripture of Mañjuśrī on the Pure Vinaya), one fascicle; translated on the thirtieth day of the ninth month in the sixth year of the Taishi era; one manuscript copy exists.

The *Yunjing lü jing* (Cloud-Pure Vinaya Sūtra), one fascicle; translated on the eighth day of the fourth month in the tenth year of the Taikang era. The *Chujue zongchi jing* (Sūtra of the Decisive Realization of Total Retention), one fascicle;

the *Baonü jing* (Sūtra of the Jewel Maiden), four fascicles—the old catalogs refer to it as the *Baonü sanmei jing* (Sūtra of the Jewel Maiden’s Samādhi) or the *Baonü wenhui jing* (Sūtra of the Jewel Maiden’s Inquiry into Wisdom);

translated on the twenty-seventh day of the fourth month in the eighth year of the Taikang era. The *Rulai xingxian jing* (Sūtra of the Manifestation of the Tathāgata), four fascicles; one version states: [translated on the same date].
The *Xingxian Ruhuan jing* (Sūtra on the Manifestation of Illusion) was translated on the twenty-fifth day of the twelfth month of the first year of the Yuankang era.

On the same day, two fascicles of the *Banzhou sanmei jing* (Pratyutpanna Samādhi Sūtra) were produced. Master Dao’an’s catalogue states that there is also a separate translation of the *Banzhou sanmei jing*, namely the one-fascicle *Shouyi nü jing* (Sūtra of the Maiden Shouyi), also known as the *Fannü shouyi jing* (Sūtra of the Brahmin Maiden Shouyi).
Furthermore, there are the one-fascicle *Shier yinyuan jing* (Sūtra of the Twelve Links of Dependent Origination) and the *Yueming tongzi jing* (Sūtra of the Youth Candraprabha).
One fascicle; also titled *The Scripture of the Youth Candraprabha*. *The Scripture on the Fifty Circumstantial Practices of the Body*, one fascicle;

the old catalogues state it is also called *The Scripture on the Fifty Matters of the Bodhisattva’s Circumstantial Body* or *The Scripture on the Bodhisattva’s Practice of the Fifty Circumstantial Bodies*.
*The Scripture on the Sixty-two Views*, one fascicle; also called *The Brahmajāla Scripture on the Sixty-two Views*. *The Scripture on the Four Self-Inflicted Injuries*, one fascicle.
Master Dao’an stated that the *Abhidharma Sumati Sūtra* in one fascicle was translated;
the old catalogs call it the *Sumati Sūtra* or the *Sumati Bodhisattva Sūtra*, while the *Suiquan Nü Sūtra* in two fascicles appears in the *Bie lu*.

Master Dao’an’s catalog does not list the *Vaipulya Nirvāṇa Sūtra* in two fascicles—also called the *Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra*—which appeared on the second day of the seventh month in the fifth year of the Taishi era.
On the thirteenth day, the *Mahā-upāya-kauśalya-sūtra* in two fascicles was translated;

it is also called the *Sūtra on the Great Skillful Means Asked by Bodhisattva Prajñottara*, the *Sūtra of Bodhisattva Prajñottara*, the *Sūtra of Skillful Means*, or the *Sūtra on the Infinite [Virtue] of Deliverance through Skillful Means*.
On the seventeenth day of the sixth month of the sixth year of Taikang, the *Anabhilāpya-śrīkumāra-bodhisattva-sūtra* was translated.
*Sūtra* (one fascicle), also known as the *Sūtra of the Bodhisattva of Wordlessness*. *The Sūtra of the Warm Bath* (one fascicle);
the old catalogues state it is the *Sūtra on the Warm Bath for the Assembly of Monks*. *The Sūtra of the Crown King* (one fascicle); also named the *Sūtra of the Questions of Vipaśyin*.
Master Dao’an states it is from the Vaipulya section; others say it is the *Mahāvaipulya Sūtra of the Crown King*. *The Sūtra of the Holy Dharma Seal* (one fascicle). Translated in India.
Titled *Acāramā* (also known as the *Tu'ang Gong*); it is said to be the one-fascicle *Sūtra on Moving Mountains from the Saṃyukta Āgama*.
The old catalogs list it as the *Sūtra on the Malla Moving Mountains*. Also, the one-fascicle *Sūtra on Mañjuśrī’s Repentance with the Five Limbs*;

the old catalogs list it as the *Sūtra on Mañjuśrī’s Repentance*. Also, the three-fascicle *Sūtra on the Bodhisattva Dharaṇīdhara*. Also, the one-fascicle *Sūtra on Extinguishing the Darkness of the Ten Directions*.
One fascicle. Translated on the fourteenth day of the eighth month in the first year of the Yuánxī era. *Wúsìyì háitóng jīng* (The Sutra of the Inconceivable Child).
The old catalogues state that this is also called the *Háitóng jīng*, or the *Wúsìyìguāng háitóng púsà jīng*, or the *Wúsìyìguāng jīng*.
One fascicle. *Jiāshè jíjié jīng* (The Sutra Compiled by Kāśyapa). The old catalogues state that this is also called the *Jiāshè jié jīng*. [The section on] Maitreya’s Attainment.

*Fó jīng* (Buddha Sūtra), one fascicle; a different version from that translated by Kumārajīva; *Shèlìfú Mùlián yóu zhū guó jīng* (Sūtra on Śāriputra and Maudgalyāyana Traveling Through Various Countries), one fascicle—also called *Shèlìfú Mó Mùqiéluán yóu zhū sìqú jīng* (Sūtra on Śāriputra and Mahāmaudgalyāyana Traveling Through the Four Crossroads); *Líulíwáng jīng* (Sūtra of King Vairāṭa), one fascicle;
*Nàinǚ Qíyù jīng* (Sūtra of the Woman Nàinǚ and Jīvaka), one fascicle—also called *Nàinǚ jīng* (Sūtra of the Woman Nàinǚ); *Bǎoshìnǚ jīng* (Sūtra of the Woman Ratnadattā), one fascicle.
*The Scripture of the Youth Ratnajālin*, one fascicle; the old catalog states it is the *Ratnajāla Sūtra*. *The Scripture on Accordance with Expedient Means*, two fascicles;

one version states it is the *Scripture on Solely Expedient Means*. The old catalog states it is the *Scripture of the Girl Accordance with Expedient Means*, also known as the *Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Transformation of Female Form*.
*The Scripture on the Original Arisings of the Five Hundred Disciples*, one fascicle; the old catalog states it is the *Self-[Arising] of the Five Hundred Disciples*.

The *Shuobenmo jing* (Sutra on Explaining Origins and Ends), also known as the *Fowubai dizizi zishuo benqi jing* (Sutra of the Five Hundred Disciples of the Buddha Speaking of Their Own Past Lives) or the *Fo wei pusa wumen jing* (Sutra of the Five Dreams of the Buddha as a Bodhisattva), one fascicle; the old catalogs refer to it as the *Fo wumen* or the *Taizi wumen*.

The *Pumen jing* (Universal Gate Sutra), one fascicle—another version calls it the *Pumen pin* (Universal Gate Chapter); it was translated on the eleventh day of the first month in the eighth year of the Taikang era. Like an illusion.
*Samādhi Sūtra*, two fascicles; the old catalog states it was three fascicles. *Maitreya’s Original Vow Sūtra*, one fascicle;
alternatively called *The Sūtra on the Original Vows Asked by Bodhisattva Maitreya*. *Śāriputra’s Repentance Sūtra*, one fascicle. *Womb Sūtra*, one fascicle;
the old catalog calls it *The Sūtra on Receiving a Body in the Womb*. *Daśabhūmika Sūtra*, one fascicle; alternatively called *The Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva*.
*The Sūtra on the Former Life of Maudgalyāyana*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of Prince Mubao*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Four Unobtainables*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of the Bodhisattva’s Repentance*, one fascicle (also titled *The Dharma of the Bodhisattva’s Repentance*; the sub-note states it is extracted from Nāgārjuna’s *Daśabhūmivibhāṣā-śāstra*);
*The Sūtra of Future Transformations*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Radiance of Milk*, one fascicle; *The Woman of the Heart-Mantra*.
*The Sūtra on the Brahmin’s Wife Offering Rice Gruel*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra of the Heart-Mantra*. *The Sūtra on the Sixfold Prostration*, one fascicle;
the old catalogs call it *The Sūtra on the Sixfold Prostration*, or *The Sūtra on the Sixfold Prostration of the Elder Weihua*.
*The Aṅgulimāla Sūtra*, one fascicle; also known as *The Sūtra of the Finger-Garland* or *The Sūtra of the Finger-Bun*. *The Sūtra on the Ten Stages of the Bodhisattva*, one fascicle.
*The Scripture on King Kalmāṣapāda*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Manifestation of the Six Pāramitās*, one fascicle (also known as the *Scripture on the Elephant’s Emergence*);
*The Scripture on the Illumination Samādhi*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Sufferings Brought by Desires*, one fascicle;

*The Scripture on the Exhaustion of the Dharma*, one fascicle (alternatively titled the *Scripture on the Questions of the Bodhisattva Śūnyatāśānti*); *The Ritual for the Bodhisattva Fast*, one fascicle (also known as the *One Name*).
*The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Right Fasting*, also known as *The Sutra on Maintaining the Fast* or *The Sutra on the Samādhi of Solitary Realization and Self-Vow*, one fascicle;

alternatively titled *The Tathāgata’s Sutra on the Samādhi of Solitary Realization and Self-Vow*. *The Sutra on the Almsround of Past Buddhas*, one fascicle; the old catalogues call it *The Sutra on the Almsround of Buddhas of the Past*.
*The Sutra on the Five Hindrances, Doubtful Bonds, and Loss of Practice*, one fascicle; Master Dao’an says it is not [authentic].

The *Hugong chuhou ji* (Record of What Appeared After Master Hu’s Passing) states: "On the twelfth day of the fourth month in the second year of the Yongning era, the four-fascicle *Acaomo jing* (Akṣayamati-sūtra) was translated.

Alternatively, it says: "The *Acaomo pusa jing* (Akṣayamati-bodhisattva-sūtra). According to the *Bielu* (Separate Record), the *Wuji bao jing* (Sūtra of the Treasure of the Limitless) in one fascicle was previously missing from Daoan’s record;

according to the *Bielu*, Daoan’s record was previously missing [the *Wuji bao sanmei*]. Alternatively, it says: "[Daoan’s record] was previously missing the *Wuji bao sanmei* (Samādhi of the Treasure of the Limitless)."
The *Āśudā Sūtra*, one fascicle, is recorded in the *Bielu* (Separate Catalog); it was previously missing from the An-lu (An’s Catalog).
The old catalogs state it is either the *Āśudā Daughter Sūtra* or the *Āshuda Bodhisattva Sūtra of King Aja*.
These ninety works, totaling two hundred and six fascicles, all currently exist among the extant scriptures.
The *Samantanetra-bodhisattva-sūtra* in two fascicles, as recorded in the *Bielu* (Separate Catalog), was previously missing from the An-lu (An Shigao’s Catalog).

There is also the *Xianju jing* (Sutra on Dwelling in Seclusion) in one fascicle and the *Xiaopin* (Shorter Version of the Prajñāpāramitā) in seven fascicles. Furthermore, the *Zongchi jing* (Dhāraṇī Sūtra) in one fascicle—according to Sengyou’s examination, this *Chusheng jing* (Sutra on the Origin of Life) is also called the *Foxin zongchi chaojiming jing* (Sutra of the Buddha-Mind Dhāraṇī and Transcendent Sun Radiance) in two fascicles—and the abridged *Weimojie jing* (Vimalakīrti Sūtra) in one fascicle. It is Sengyou’s opinion that these were produced earlier.

The *Vimalakīrti-vinaya-guruka-saṃgraha* (The Vimalakīrti’s Heavy Protection and Excerpted Verses) consists of stray verses. The *Tarkarī-artha-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Meaning of Tarkarī), one fascicle;

the *Aśoka-dāna-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Gift of Aśoka), one fascicle—another version states that the daughter of King Ajātaśatru was named Aśokadāna; the *Pañca-puṇya-dāna-sūtra* (The Sūtra on the Five Auspicious Gifts), one fascicle;

the *Loutan-jing* (The Loutan Sūtra), five fascicles—Master Dao’an stated it was extracted from the Vaipulya section; the *Yongfu-ting-jing* (The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Heroic Subjugation), two fascicles—Master Dao’an stated [it was translated by] An Shigao.
Furthermore, there were produced: the *Śūraṅgama-sūtra* (one fascicle), translated in the fourth month of the first year of the Yuankang era;
the *Śuddhaviśuddha-samādhi-sūtra* (one fascicle), also known as the *Xushi-jing* or the *Huiming-jing*; the *Kāśyapa-mūla-sūtra* (one fascicle);
alternatively, the *Mahākāśyapa-mūla-prabhāsa-lokendra-avalokiteśvara-mahāsthāmaprāpta-vyākaraṇa-sūtra* (one fascicle); and the *Sarvadigbuddhanāma-sūtra* (one fascicle).
*The Sūtra on Maudgalyāyana Ascending to the Śuddhāvāsa Heavens*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Youth Viśeṣamati*, one fascicle; *The Names of the Buddhas of the Ten Directions*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra on the Practice of the Three Grades*, one fascicle; Master Dao’an stated that a person of recent times combined this with the *Sūtra on Great Practice*;
*The Sūtra of the Elder’s Son Jin-yi*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Many Blessings*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra on the Four Matters of Non-deviation in Contemplative Practice*, one fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Extinction of the Lesser Dharma*, one fascicle; *The Parable of the Four Women*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of Lu-yi-hsien*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of Various Divine Spells*, three fascicles; *The Sūtra of King Aṭavika*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of Nāgadatta*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of Dānyā*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of the Horse King*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of Universal Meaning*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Mother of the Deer*, one fascicle; *The Clarification of Anāthapiṇḍada*, one fascicle.
*The Scripture on Virtue*, one fascicle; the old catalog states it is the *Sutra of the Dragon Kings, Brothers, Admonishing the King* by the Elder Anāthapiṇḍada (one fascicle);
*The Scripture on Exhorting and Transforming the King*, one fascicle; *The Names of One Hundred Buddhas*, one fascicle; additionally, the *Sutra of King Ajātaśatru*, two fascicles;
*The Scripture on Planting the Roots of All Merits*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Fruits Verified by Śramaṇas*, one fascicle.
*The Sūtra on the Original Account of the Offering by the Dragon-King* (1 scroll); the old catalogues call it *The Sūtra on the Offering by the Dragon* or *The Sūtra on the Dragon-Girl*.
*The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Repentance* (1 scroll). *The Sūtra of the Three Turnings of the Moonlight* (1 scroll). *The Sūtra on the Explanation of Impermanence* (1 scroll).
*The Womb-Treasury Sūtra* (1 scroll). *The Sūtra of the Stainless Canopy* (1 scroll). *The Minor Ugra Sūtra* (1 scroll). *Ajātaśatru* [Sūtra] (1 scroll).
*The Scripture on Women*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Merchant*, two fascicles; *The Scripture on Where People Come From*, one fascicle;

*The Scripture on Admonishing Rāhula*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Goose King*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Tenfold Treasury*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on the Goose King and His Five Hundred Geese*, one fascicle;

*The Scripture on the Requisites of Precepts*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on Resolving the Paths of the Laity and the Clergy*, one fascicle; *The Scripture on Fierce Generosity*, one fascicle. [Recorded in the Old Catalogue.]
*Yunmeng shidao ji jing* (Sutra on the Stages of the Path of Fierce Giving), one fascicle; *Qisheshou shan jie* (Explanation at Vulture Peak), one fascicle;

*Piyu sanbai shou jing* (Sutra of Three Hundred Similes), twenty-five fascicles; *Biqiuni jie jing* (Sutra of Precepts for Bhikṣuṇīs), one fascicle; *Jie wang jing* (Sutra of Admonishing the King), one fascicle;
*Sanpin huiguo jing* (Sutra of Repentance in Three Sections), one fascicle; *Pusa zhai fa* (Ritual for the Bodhisattva Fast), one fascicle. The old catalog refers to this as the *Pusa zhai jing*.
Some say that the *Xiánshǒu púsà zhāijīng* (Sutra on the Fasting Ritual of the Bodhisattva Bhadramukha) consists of sixty-four sections totaling one hundred and sixteen fascicles;
this scripture is currently missing.
Combined with the preceding item, there are two works.
In total, there were one hundred and fifty-four works,
comprising three hundred and nine fascicles,
during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty.
The śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa traveled to the Western Regions, where he obtained the Indic manuscripts and returned.
This occurred from the Taishi era until the second year of the Yongjia period of Emperor Huai.
Regarding what was previously translated,
Sengyou compiled various records;
having encountered the works produced by Master Hu, he further obtained four additional texts.
The records of Dao’an were previously missing;
they are now entered into the catalog.
Master Dao’an said:

Because the records were scattered during the chaos and there were minor errors in their transmission, we know for certain that what has now been obtained is indeed the version translated by Dharmarakṣa.

The *Chāorìmíng jīng* (Sūtra of the Sun-Transcending Radiance), two fascicles; the old catalog states: "The *Chāorìmíng sānmèi jīng* (Sūtra of the Sun-Transcending Radiance Samādhi), one part. To its right [is listed] this single volume.
In two volumes total.
Translated during the reign of Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty by the śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa.
The original Sanskrit was translated first,
but the language and meaning were cumbersome and repetitive;
Upāsaka Nie Chengyuan then revised the prose and verses, condensing them into two fascicles.

The *Sūtra of the Devaputra Susīma* in two fascicles—also known as the *Sūtra on the Four Matters Asked by the Devaputra Susīma*—was translated on the eighth day of the eleventh month in the second year of the Taishi era. This constitutes one work in two fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Wu of the Jin dynasty,
the Indian Bodhisattva Śramaṇa Dharmarakṣa orally transmitted [the text],
which was transcribed by An Wenhui and Bai Yuanshin.

The *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra* in three fascicles; the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi-sūtra* in two fascicles, recorded in the *Bielu* (Separate Catalog) but previously missing from the *Anlu* (An’s Catalog); and the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi-sūtra* in two fascicles by Shulan, recorded in the *Jiulu* (Old Catalog). These two works constitute the right-hand section.
It consists of five fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Hui of the Jin dynasty,
Zhu Shulan [translated it].
Translated in the first year of the Yuankang era.
The *Weidai pusa jing* (Sūtra of the Bodhisattva Weidai), one fascicle; this work is currently missing.
This section in total consists of one fascicle.
During the reign of Emperor Hui of the Jin dynasty, the śramaṇa Bo Fazhu translated the *Loutan jing* (Lokānuvartana-sūtra) in six fascicles, as recorded in the *Bielu*.

The *Anlu* previously lacked it. There are also four other works: the *Dafangdeng rulai zang jing* (Tathāgatagarbha-sūtra) in one fascicle; the *Faju benmo jing* (Dharmapada-mūla-sūtra) in four fascicles—also known as the *Faju yu jing* (Dharmapada-avadāna-sūtra)—which is sometimes in six fascicles or called the *Faju pi jing*; and the *Futian jing* (Puṇyakṣetra-sūtra) in one fascicle—also known as the *Zhude futian jing* (Sukṛta-puṇyakṣetra-sūtra). These constitute the four sections.
It consists of twelve fascicles in total.
It was translated by the śramaṇa Dharmakṣema during the reigns of Emperors Huai and Hui of the Jin dynasty.
The *Dharmapada* and the *Sūtra on Similes for the Field of Merit* were translated together by Zhu Fakuang and the śramaṇa Falì; these,
along with the previously produced scriptures, constitute the total.
From An Shigao below up to Falì above,
there are seventeen schools in total;
all are recorded in the catalog compiled by Master An.
As for Zhang Qian, Qin Jing, Zhu Shuofo, Weizhinan, Zhu Jiangyan, Bai Yan, and Bo Fazhu—
these seven individuals were appended by Sengyou to the various records based on newly acquired materials.
The portions following the *Shi weishi du* (The Crossing by the Guardian) were all newly compiled by Zhi Yao.

Regarding the two fascicles of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra on the Practice of the Way* (*Dàoxíng jīng*), various catalogs state that these two fascicles of the *Dàoxíng jīng* were a brief excerpt produced by the Guardian; they are now missing. This constitutes one section.
It consists of two fascicles in total.
It was translated by the lay practitioner (weishi) Dulu during the reign of Emperor Hui of the Jin dynasty.

The *Vimalakīrtinirdeśa-sūtra* in five fascicles, combining the three versions produced by Zhi Qian, Zhu Fahu, and Zhu Shulan, is unified into one work. The *Śūraṅgama-samādhi-sūtra* in eight fascicles, combining the four versions produced by Zhi Yao, Zhi Qian, Zhu Fahu, and Zhu Shulan, is unified into one work, which may consist of five fascicles. These two works are as follows.
It consists of thirteen fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Hui of the Jin dynasty,
the śramaṇa Zhi Mindu compiled it, combining the various versions of the *Śūraṃgama-samādhi*.
The tradition states that the collection compiled by Yan Min-du was incomplete;

it is noted that its authenticity remains uncertain. One fascicle of the *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-dhāraṇī* and one fascicle of the *Mahāmāyūrī-miśra-vidyārājñī-dhāraṇī*: these two sections [are as follows].
Two fascicles.
Translated during the reign of Emperor Yuan of the Jin dynasty by the eminent śramaṇa Śrīmitra from the Western Regions.
The *Dṛṣṭānta-sūtra* (Piyu jing), ten fascicles; the old catalogues state it is the *Saddṛṣṭānta-sūtra* (Zheng piyu jing), ten fascicles. This one work consists of ten fascicles in total.
It was [translated] during the reign of Emperor Cheng of the Jin dynasty.
The śramaṇa Kang Fashui excerpted and compiled from various sūtras to compose this single work:
one fascicle of the *Śāriputra-vinaya Bhikṣu-prātimokṣa-sūtra*, also known as the *Mahābhikṣu-prātimokṣa of the Daśabhāṇavāra*. This constitutes one section.
One fascicle in total.
During the reign of Emperor Jianwen of the Jin dynasty, the Western Region śramaṇa Dharma... [The text continues with the name of the translator, likely Dharmakṣema or a similar transliteration.]
One fascicle of the *Bhikṣuṇī-mahā-śīla-sūtra*, held in its Hu (Central Asian) original and translated by Zhu Fonian. This constitutes one work.
One fascicle in total.
During the reign of Emperor Jianwen of the Jin dynasty,
the śramaṇa Shi Sengchun [compiled this].
The original Indic manuscript was obtained in the kingdom of Kuci in the Western Regions.
Upon arriving in Guanzhong, Zhu Fonian, Dharmagupta, and Huichang jointly translated it.

This is the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra-śāstra* in five fascicles, also known as the *Chang'an-pin jing* or the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra*, produced during the eighteenth year of the Jianyuan era of Fu Jian of the Later Qin. This constitutes one work.
It consists of five fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Jianwen of the Jin dynasty,
the Indian śramaṇa Dharmapriya...
The *Mahāprajñāpāramitā-sūtra* (Hú Dàpǐn Běn) was translated by Zhu Fóniàn from a manuscript brought from the Hu region.

The *Saṃyuktābhidharma-vibhāṣā-śāstra*, fourteen fascicles, was produced beginning on the fourth day of the fourth month in the nineteenth year of the Jiànyuán era of the pseudo-Qin dynasty and completed on the twenty-ninth day of the eighth month; some say it is the *Saṃyuktābhidharma-hṛdaya-śāstra*, ten fascicles, by Vasumitra, which was produced beginning on the fifteenth day of the third month in the twentieth year of the Jiànyuán era and completed on the thirteenth day of the seventh month. The *Saṃgharakṣa-saṃyukta-sūtra*, three fascicles, was produced on the thirtieth day of the eleventh month in the twentieth year of the Jiànyuán era of the Qin dynasty. These are the three aforementioned works.
It consists of twenty-seven fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Jin dynasty,
the Kasmirian śramaṇa Saṃghabhūti...
During the time of Fu Jian, he entered Chang’an;
Sanghavarman recited it orally, and Buddharakṣa translated it.
Furthermore, he brought the original Sanskrit manuscript of the *Vasumitra*, which Zhu Fonian translated.
This consists of two fascicles of the *Sectarian Compilation of the Four Āgamas* (Sīfēn āhán mù chāo jīng); this constitutes one work.
It consists of two fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Jin dynasty,
the Śramaṇa Kumārabuddhi from the Western Regions [translated it].
It was produced at Ye Monastery.
Buddhabhadra held the Hu (foreign) manuscript,
while Zhu Fonian and Fotudeng acted as translators.
Sengdao acted as the oral reciter and Sengrui as the scribe.

One fascicle of the *Saptatriṃśat-dharmapada-sūtra*, translated in the sixth month of the year Wuchen (the thirty-seventh year of the Taiyuan era of the Jin dynasty). One fascicle of the *Bhadrakalpa-sahasra-buddha-nāma-sūtra*. The above consists of two works.
It consists of two fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Jin dynasty,
the Indian śramaṇa Zhu Tanwulan [translated it].
Compiled at Xiezhengxi Monastery in Yangzhou.

The *Ekottarika Āgama* (Zēngyī Āhán Jīng), thirty-three fascicles, was produced during the summer of the twentieth year of the Jianyuan era of the Qin dynasty and completed in the spring of the twenty-first year; it is fixed at thirty-three fascicles, though sometimes divided into twenty-four sections. The *Madhyama Āgama* (Zhōng Āhán Jīng), fifty-nine fascicles, was produced in the twentieth year of the Jianyuan era of the Zhou dynasty. These two collections are as follows.
It consists of ninety-two fascicles.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Jin dynasty,
the śramaṇa Dharmalan-di from the country of Tukhāra [translated it].
During the reign of Fu Jian, he entered Chang’an;
Nandī recited the text from the Hu (foreign) original,
and Zhu Fonian translated it out.

The *Chuyao jing* (Udānavarga) in nineteen fascicles; the *Pusa yingluo jing* (Bodhisattvālaṃkāra-sūtra) in twelve fascicles; the *Shizhu duanjie jing* (Daśabhūmika-vibhaṅga-sūtra) in eleven fascicles; the *Pusa chutai jing* (Bodhisattvagarbha-sūtra) in five fascicles—also known as the *Taijing* or in four fascicles; the *Zhongyin jing* (Antarābhava-sūtra) in two fascicles; and the *Wangzi fayi huaimu yinyuan jing* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of Prince Fayi’s Loss of Sight), also called the *Ayuwang xi huaimu yinyuan jing* (Sūtra on the Causes and Conditions of King Aśoka’s Son Losing His Sight)—these six works.
It consists of fifty fascicles in total.
During the reign of Emperor Xiaowu of the Jin dynasty,
the śramaṇa Zhu Fonian of Liangzhou [translated it].
It was translated in Guanzhong during the time of Fu Jian.

The *Madhyamāgama* in sixty fascicles was translated at Dongting Temple on the tenth day of the eleventh month of the first year of the Long’an era of the Jin dynasty, and completed on the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month of the second year; it differs greatly from that produced by Dharmasatya. The *Abhidharma-aṣṭagrantha* in twenty fascicles, also known as the *Kātyāyanīputra-abhidharma*, was produced in the nineteenth year of the Jianyuan era. The *Abhidharmahṛdaya* in sixteen (or thirteen) fascicles was produced in Luoyang at the end of the Jianyuan era under Fu Jian. The *Vibhāṣā-abhidharma* in fourteen fascicles, also known as the *Vistara*, was likewise translated in Luoyang. The *Abhidharmahṛdaya* in four fascicles was translated for Master Huiyuan at Mount Lu in the sixteenth year of the Taiyuan era of the Jin dynasty. The *Tridharmaka* in two fascicles was also produced at Mount Lu in the sixteenth year of the Taiyuan era. These comprise the six works listed above.
It consists of one hundred and sixteen fascicles.
It was translated during the reigns of Emperor Xiaowu and Emperor An of the Jin dynasty by the Kasmirian śramaṇa Saṃghadeva.

The New Mahāprajñāpāramitā Sūtra in twenty-four fascicles was translated at the Xiaoyao Garden on the twenty-second day of the fourth month in the fifth year of the Hongshi era of Yao Xing of the pseudo-Qin dynasty, and was completed on the twenty-third day of the fourth month in the sixth year.
The New Aṣṭasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra in seven fascicles was translated from the sixth day of the second month to the twentieth day of the fourth month in the tenth year of the Hongshi era.
